EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces significant escalation as direct military confrontations between the US and Iran intensify, evidenced by Iranian missile strikes damaging US aircraft in Jordan and US destruction of Iranian tankers. Simultaneously, the IAEA has referred Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council, and Houthi forces have made strategic gains in Yemen, capturing the port city of Mokha, fueling a sharp rise in regional oil prices and increasing the risk of wider conflict.

IRAN
Iran received air defense systems, medicine, vehicles, and communication equipment worth millions of dollars from China in the past year, facilitated by an oil-for-credit mechanism to circumvent sanctions. The IAEA Board of Governors approved a resolution referring Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council for non-compliance with the NPT, a decision Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned as "contradictory, baseless," and politically motivated, noting that approximately one-third of IAEA member states opposed or abstained. Iran's UN representative, Gholamhossein Darzi, called US sanctions on 27 Iranian companies "economic terrorism." IRGC spokesman Mohibi outlined six conditions for ending the conflict, including a complete cessation of hostilities, Israel's withdrawal from Lebanon, an end to the Yemen blockade, and the release of $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets. CNN satellite analysis revealed a surge in construction activity at Iran's deeply buried "Pickaxe Mountain" site near Natanz, suspected to be a future nuclear facility, drawing a stern warning from US President Trump. Iranian media reported explosions on Qeshm Island, near Sirik, and Jask, with some sources suggesting these were due to missile clashes at sea. The US Central Command refuted IRGC claims of hitting US Navy destroyers, stating all IRGC attacks failed, while US forces successfully destroyed 10 Iranian tankers in the last week, which they claim were part of a "multibillion-dollar shadow network" funding the IRGC. Iran's First Vice President Aref criticized the IAEA resolution as demonstrating double standards. Iran's Minister of Defense issued a statement suggesting imminent military developments: "To the extent of Iran, from the depths of the earth to the heights of the sky, you will soon see..."

ISRAEL
The IDF and Shin Bet destroyed three Hamas weapon depots in different areas of the Gaza Strip, which stored firearms, explosive devices, and anti-tank rockets. The IDF killed Farah Hamed, a senior commander in Hamas's military wing, in an Israeli strike in Gaza City's Sheikh Ijlin neighborhood. Hamed was a member of the "Silwad cell" and was deported to Gaza in 2011 as part of the Gilad Shalit prisoner exchange deal. Israeli forces conducted strikes in the Gaza City's Shati camp and Khan Yunis, resulting in casualties. In the West Bank, the IDF arrested three Palestinian Authority police officers for illegally setting up a blockade in Area C near Beitunia, detaining and assaulting an off-duty Israeli reservist, an act the IDF described as a "serious overreach." Colonel Omri Meshiach, commander of the Northern Brigade, stated that the IDF completed the destruction of tunnels in Beit Hanoun and stressed the importance of the "Yellow Line" for protecting Israeli communities. Air raid sirens were activated in northern Israel (Ghajar, Kfar Yuval, Ma'ayan Baruch, HaGoshrim, Beit Hillel) due to a hostile aircraft intrusion, later confirmed as a false alarm. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu visited the Syrian Hermon, stating Israel is "very close" to defeating the Iranian regime and will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders. Defense Minister stated, "We struck Iran twice. When needed, we will strike a third time."

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF and Shin Bet operations destroyed three Hamas weapon depots across the Gaza Strip. Farah Hamed, a senior Hamas military wing commander and a member of the al-Qassam Brigades' Military Council in the West Bank, was killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza City's Sheikh Ijlin neighborhood. The strike followed a warning from the military and reports of a drone attack in Khan Yunis injuring three. Civil Defense teams recovered four bodies from the Ahmed family after their home in the Beit Lahia Project in northern Gaza was bombed. In the West Bank, Israeli forces killed a 29-year-old Palestinian man in Aqraba, Nablus, and withheld his body. Six Palestinians were abducted, and homes were damaged during an Israeli raid in Tulkarm. Three Palestinian Authority police officers were arrested by the IDF for an unauthorized blockade in Area C of the West Bank, where they allegedly detained and assaulted an Israeli reservist. Sabah Haniyeh, sister of the late Hamas political bureau chief, is slated to testify in court on charges of incitement and identifying with a terror organization.

LEBANON
Lebanese media reported an Israeli strike on a motorcycle between the towns of Harouf and Zebdin in southern Lebanon, killing one person. Multiple Israeli airstrikes were reported in southern Lebanon, specifically in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, Al-Qantara, Al-Mansouri, Bani Hiyan, and Saroubin. The sounds of explosions are expected to be heard in Israel's Upper Galilee region due to these ongoing strikes. Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned Israel's aggression against Lebanon, particularly attacks on residential areas, and the IRGC spokesman included Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon as a condition for ending the wider regional conflict.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu visited the Syrian Hermon (Mount Sheikh), emphasizing Israel's control over the area and its determination not to allow any terrorist army to establish itself on its borders. Reports indicated Israeli artillery shelled northern parts of Tarnejeh village near Quneitra. At least 14 people were killed in an ammunition depot explosion in Idlib, northern Syria. In Iraq, a Panama-flagged tanker carrying 2 million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil was struck by a drone in Iraqi territorial waters near the port of Fao. Port officials confirmed the fire was extinguished, with no casualties reported. An armed attack in Missan province, southern Iraq, resulted in two deaths.

GULF STATES
Houthi forces have reportedly achieved a significant strategic victory by capturing the port city of Mokha, including its main port and airport, expanding their control over 2,500 square kilometers of Yemen's Red Sea coast and near the critical Bab al-Mandab Strait. Saudi Arabia confirmed Houthi attacks on cities in its southwestern region, including Khamis Mushait and Abha, triggering emergency alerts and reportedly halting air operations at King Abdulaziz Airport in Jeddah and Abha Airport. Saudi Air Force responded with over 40 airstrikes against Houthi forces in Hodeidah, Taiz, Marib, Al Jawf, and Saada. Satellite images show significant damage to Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery. Pakistan delivered a warning from Saudi Arabia to Iran, urging Tehran to curb Houthi attacks on the Kingdom, emphasizing that aggression on Saudi territory could activate a defense pact involving Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia. An Iranian official stated Iran does not control the Houthis, but two Iranian sources claimed Tehran ordered the Houthi attacks last week and provided additional funding and weapons, with IRGC commanders traveling to Yemen. Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has decreased, with only 7 vessels on Wednesday compared to a 10-day average of 14. A suspected attack on a ship near Port Rashid in Dubai was reported by the UKMTO. Yemeni President Mahdi Al-Mashat offered a presidential pardon to Houthi opponents in the western coastal fronts who lay down their arms.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Houthi Seizure of Mokha:** Houthi forces have reportedly captured the strategic port city of Mokha in Yemen, including its main port and airport, significantly expanding their control over the Red Sea coast and near the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
2.  **US-Iran Military Escalation:** Iranian ballistic missile strikes on the Muwaffaq Salti air base in Jordan reportedly damaged multiple US military aircraft, including one A-10 Thunderbolt and eight F-15s. The US Central Command claimed its forces destroyed 10 Iranian tankers in the last week, asserting that all IRGC attacks against US warships failed.
3.  **IAEA Refers Iran to UNSC:** The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Board of Governors approved a resolution referring Iran's nuclear program to the UN Security Council for non-compliance with the NPT, a first in 20 years.
4.  **Oil Prices Soar and Currency Weakens:** Brent crude surpassed $100 a barrel for the first time since July, and the Iranian Rial weakened significantly, with the dollar reaching 235,000 IRR, amid heightened regional tensions and the Iran-US conflict.
5.  **Pakistan Mediates Saudi-Houthi Conflict:** Pakistan conveyed a warning from Saudi Arabia to Iran to curb Houthi attacks on the Kingdom, indicating that strikes on Saudi territory could activate a defense pact with Turkey and Pakistan.
6.  **Targeting of Iran's "Pickaxe Mountain" Site:** CNN satellite analysis revealed a surge in construction activity at Iran's deeply buried "Pickaxe Mountain" site near Natanz, which the US suspects to be a nuclear facility. US President Trump warned Iran against "trying to be smart" there.
7.  **Israeli Operations in Gaza and Lebanon:** Israeli forces destroyed three Hamas weapon depots and killed Farah Hamed, a senior Hamas military commander, in Gaza. Multiple Israeli airstrikes were also reported in southern Lebanon.
8.  **Tanker Attacks in Gulf Waters:** A Panama-flagged tanker carrying Iraqi fuel oil was struck by a drone in Iraqi territorial waters, and a suspected attack occurred on a ship near Port Rashid in Dubai.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The current situation carries a high risk of escalation, driven by direct US-Iran military engagements, including US aircraft damage and US destruction of Iranian tankers, and aggressive rhetoric from both sides. The Strait of Hormuz and wider Persian Gulf remain critical flashpoints, marked by reduced shipping traffic, alleged tanker attacks, and Iran's stated conditions for ending the conflict. In Yemen, the Houthi capture of Mokha and ongoing attacks on Saudi cities, coupled with intense Saudi aerial responses, risk broadening the conflict, potentially involving the Pakistan-Turkey-Saudi defense pact. Israel's northern border with Lebanon remains volatile due to ongoing Israeli strikes. The "Pickaxe Mountain" nuclear site in Iran represents a potential red line for the US.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** maintained a confrontational posture, with President Trump warning Iran against activities at "Pickaxe Mountain" and claiming further strikes on Iranian tankers. Senior advisors reportedly cautioned Trump that the war might extend beyond 2029. **Pakistan**, mediating for Saudi Arabia, warned Iran about Houthi attacks, highlighting a potential activation of its defense pact with **Turkey** and **Saudi Arabia**. **China** continued its economic ties with Iran, providing sanctioned goods via an oil-for-credit system, and joined **Russia** in rejecting the IAEA resolution against Iran. Saudi Arabia conducted extensive airstrikes in Yemen and faced Houthi missile attacks on its cities and infrastructure. The **United Kingdom**, along with the US, France, and Germany, led the IAEA resolution against Iran, with its Foreign Minister not ruling out sanctions on Israeli banks. **Germany** pledged continued support for Ukraine, while its Chancellor criticized the far-right AfD for pro-Russian stances. Other **Gulf States**, including UAE and Qatar, welcomed British and European sanctions against Israeli settlements.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Reporting contains **contradictions** regarding Iran's control over the Houthis; an Iranian official claimed no control, while other Iranian sources indicated Tehran ordered Houthi attacks and provided support. There are **conflicting accounts** of US-Iran military engagements, with CENTCOM denying IRGC claims of hitting US warships and asserting all IRGC attacks failed, while US forces destroyed 10 Iranian tankers. **Unverified claims** abound, particularly concerning explosions in Iran (Qeshm, Sirik, Jask) and alleged damage to Saudi infrastructure (King Fahd Air Base, Jazan refinery), with varying attributions (missile clashes at sea, US aggression). **Propaganda indicators** are evident in statements from both the US (Trump's swift victory claims, oil price attributions) and Iran (IRGC's maximalist demands, claims of strategic damage to the US). There are **reporting gaps** regarding specific details of casualties and real-time verification of territorial control shifts in Yemen. The exact nature of the drone threat to Zelenskyy's plane in Moldova was also clarified from a "near-miss" to a "suspicion of drones" causing airspace closure.
